title: Prepositional 1: Where? (After 'в')
description: After 'в' (in/at), the noun shifts into the prepositional case. Most nouns take -е; nouns ending in -ия (Россия) take -ии.
descriptionRussian: После 'в' существительное переходит в предложный падеж. Большинство существительных принимают -е; существительные на -ия (Россия) принимают -ии.
intro: After the accusative, this case will feel almost unfair. Nearly every noun you meet takes the same ending regardless of gender, and there is very little to choose between. It also happens to answer the question a beginner needs answered most often, which is where something or someone is. Two lessons from now you will be able to place yourself, your friends and your things anywhere in a city. That is a lot of return for one letter.
rules: The prepositional case (предложный падеж) is the case of LOCATION (and also of topics, which we'll meet later). It always appears with a preposition; today's preposition is 'в' (in / at).
Masculine nouns ending in a hard consonant add -е in the prepositional: магазин → в магазине, дом → в доме, парк → в парке.
Feminine nouns ending in -а swap -а for -е: школа → в школе, Москва → в Москве, комната → в комнате.
Neuter nouns ending in -о swap -о for -е: окно → в окне, письмо → в письме, кафе stays as is (indeclinable).
Feminine nouns ending in -ия take -ии in the prepositional: Россия → в России, Англия → в Англии, Италия → в Италии. Country names ending in -ия all follow this pattern.
examples: Я в магазине. (I am at the store.) магазин → в магазине, masc + -е.
Маша в школе. (Masha is at school.) школа → в школе, fem -а → -е.
Антон в парке. (Anton is in the park.) парк → в парке, masc + -е.
Они в Москве. (They are in Moscow.) Москва → в Москве, fem -а → -е.
Книга в письме. (The book mention is in the letter.) письмо → в письме, neuter -о → -е.
Маша живёт в России. (Masha lives in Russia.) Россия → в России, -ия → -ии.
Антон работает в Англии. (Anton works in England.) Англия → в Англии, -ия → -ии.

items.hint: What ending does a masculine consonant noun take after 'в'?
items.explanation: After 'в' (location), Russian shifts the noun into the prepositional case. Masculine consonant nouns add -е: магазин → в магазине. The case is called 'prepositional' because it always appears with a preposition.

items.hint: Feminine -а changes to which letter in the prepositional?
items.explanation: Feminine -а changes to -е in the prepositional: школа → в школе. Notice that this is similar to the dative ending; for feminine -а, the dative and prepositional forms coincide. Context (the preposition 'в,' the meaning 'at school') tells you it is prepositional.

items.promptEnglish: The cat is in the window.
items.hint: Окно is neuter -о. What does -о become in the prepositional?
items.explanation: Neuter nouns ending in -о swap -о for -е in the prepositional, just like feminine -а: окно → в окне. The headline rule is 'most nouns take -е'; neuter -о fits that rule.

items.hint: Москва is feminine -а. What does -а become?
items.explanation: Names of cities follow the same rule. Москва is feminine -а: -а → -е → в Москве. The form does not change because Москва is a name; it changes because the case rule applies to all feminine -а nouns.

items.hint: Офис ends in a consonant. Apply the masculine rule.
items.explanation: Офис → в офисе. The pattern -consonant + -е holds across all masculine inanimate location nouns.

items.hint: Россия ends in -ия. This is the special pattern: -ия → -ии.
items.explanation: Country names ending in -ия take -ии (not -е) in the prepositional: Россия → в России. The same pattern works for all -ия names: в Англии, в Италии, в Испании. Country names come up often, so this exception is worth memorizing now.

blanks: Я живу в _____. (I live in a house.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Дом is masculine consonant. After 'в' (location), prepositional adds -е → доме.

errorCorrection.explanation: After в meaning location, the noun takes the prepositional case, and masculine consonant nouns add -е: в банке. Банк is the bare nominative (dictionary form), which can only be a subject.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is in the apartment now.
errorCorrection.explanation: After в for location, feminine -а nouns swap -а for -е: в квартире. Квартиру is the accusative, which follows в only for direction with a verb of motion ('Маша идёт в квартиру'). With no motion, the location reading requires the prepositional.

Country names ending in -ия take -ии in the prepositional, not -е: в Англии. Англие is the trap a learner produces by applying the regular -е ending, but the -ия subset blocks it and uses -ии instead. The same -ии pattern holds for в России, в Италии, в Испании.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'в' (location), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: магазине. The nominative магазин would only be a subject: 'Магазин закрыт' (The store is closed).
After 'в' (location), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: школе. The nominative школа would be a subject: 'Школа большая' (The school is big).

reviewVocab.definition: prepositional case (always used with a preposition; answers 'Где?' for location and 'О чём?' for topics)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша в школе' слово 'школе' стоит в предложном падеже.
